result.lens: method and circularity (no camera opened; existing flash_run1_repositioned data re-analysed with timing/scripts/flash_verify_method.py)

verdicts.claim: Ground truth is a QPC timecode displayed on monitor 0
verdicts.reason: No timecode is displayed. flash_timecode.cpp shows a full-screen PRNG black/white sequence and logs DXGI vblank QPC times (SyncQPCTime), linearised as a + P*refresh. The GT is the exposure start of the ROI pixels, w = T - E(1-f) or T - E*f, built from a step-display model. Scan-out, LCD response, rolling-shutter row, exposure midpoint and DWM composition are not modelled and all land in a per-camera, per-ROI constant. Independent flip on the rotated, non-primary monitor was never verified.
verdicts.numbers: 468 stats samples / 2160 presents, vblank fit resid 10 us, refresh_glitches 0, 1 disjoint

verdicts.claim: Per-frame error std vs GT: C930e uvc_pts_mapped_direct 0.52 ms, lsq_envelope 0.48 ms; C922 0.45 / 0.50 ms (i.e. PTS timestamps accurate to ~0.5 ms)
verdicts.reason: The numbers reproduce exactly. flash_analyze sets the GT reference to the best-scoring source (lsq_envelope) and tunes gamma on it, so that source's score is self-referential. With a GT that uses no device timestamp (frame index + arrival envelope, gamma fixed at 2.2) the numbers are similar. But the error depends strongly on the brightness fraction f (corr -0.76/-0.85 rising, +0.64/+0.85 falling), and fitting PTS directly to the GT still leaves 0.49/0.59 ms. So ~0.5 ms is the method's floor on real data, not the timestamp error. A synthetic perfectly periodic clock scores the same. The ranking among the PTS variants (0.45 vs 0.48 vs 0.52) means nothing.
verdicts.numbers: independent GT: mapped_direct 531/589 us, seq_periodic_env 531/584 us, pts_nominal_clock 552/589 us; GT-fitted PTS (circular) 489/588 us; gamma=1.0 -> 1.7 ms all PTS sources; between-block independent GT noise ~135 us

verdicts.claim: uvc_pts_mapped_direct mapping is not circular
verdicts.reason: The mapping is a lower-envelope line (free offset and slope) per camera, fitted against host_arrival over the whole run. The GT is not used. It is non-causal, though: online and holdout versions are worse, badly so for the C930e, whose minimum arrival latency is 22.9 ms higher for the first 2 s.
verdicts.numbers: C930e: first-half fit evaluated on second half 3.6 ms; causal envelope 2.7 ms; robust causal (per-second minima, start-up rejected) 0.61 ms. C922: causal 0.59 ms, robust causal 0.60 ms, first-half holdout 1.13 ms (n=16)

verdicts.claim: host_arrival 4.50/4.66 ms, MF os_timestamp 4.55/4.83 ms per-frame std vs GT
verdicts.reason: These are the vs-GT numbers, with the same median-only offset removal as the PTS sources. They hold under the independent GT (5.06/4.66 ms host, 5.13/4.75 ms MF). Host arrival does carry several ms of jitter. The self-selected per_frame host numbers (2.5 ms) are biased low by truncation, and the claim correctly did not use them.
verdicts.numbers: independent GT host 5063/4657 us, os 5129/4752 us

verdicts.claim: uvc_pts_mapped_direct offsets agree to 0.02 ms across cameras -> best source for multi-camera sync
verdicts.reason: The quoted -52.08/-52.10 are coarse correlation offsets on a 0.02 ms search grid. The GT median offsets differ by 0.064 ms (CI95 -0.10..0.27) or 0.19 ms (independent GT, CI95 -0.04..0.32). host_arrival also agrees (0.10 ms), so the agreement does not pick out a best source. Within one camera the offset changes by 35 ms across image blocks (rolling shutter plus scan-out, about 31 ms per frame height and 19-25 ms per frame width), and the two auto-ROIs sit at different rows and columns, so the agreement is set by ROI geometry. An online mapping shifts the cross-camera difference to -0.30 ms (robust causal) or +4.1 ms (plain causal).
verdicts.numbers: block offsets C922 -78.6..-43.2 ms, C930e -76.9..-41.1 ms; geometry fit residual 0.5/1.2 ms

verdicts.claim: No dropped frames (891/893)
verdicts.reason: In the analysed frames, the PTS slot index equals seq for both cameras, with 0 gaps. The analyze_frames drops_est of 27-30 for host/os on the C930e is an artefact: the periodogram locked onto 32.42 fps.
verdicts.numbers: pts_slot_gaps 0, 0

verdicts.claim: Method floor on synthetic data ~75 us
verdicts.reason: selftest_flash_analyze.json does give 74.8 us at zero injected noise. But the synthetic world matches the model exactly (step display, pure power-law tone curve, exact E). The real data shows f-dependent model errors of up to about 1 ms, so the real floor is about 0.5 ms.
verdicts.numbers: 75 us synthetic vs ~490-590 us real (GT-fitted PTS residual)

verdicts.claim: periodic-fit residual (analyze_frames) indicates accuracy
verdicts.reason: The residual measures only how regular a source is against its own fitted a+P*n. The C930e PTS scores 2.2 us and the C922 PTS 137 us, yet both are equal against the GT. For C930e host/os the fit has the wrong period (32.42 fps).
verdicts.numbers: C930e PTS 2.2 us, C922 PTS 137 us periodic residual

verdicts.claim: Units/clock domains consistent; device clock from descriptors
verdicts.reason: QPC runs at 10 MHz, so ns = ticks*100 and display, MF and arrival times share one domain; that checks out. But dwClockFrequency is never read; the nominal rate is guessed (30 MHz C930e, 300 MHz C922; nominal_assumed=true). The GT-derived PTS rates are +35 ppm (C930e) and -3.9 ppm (C922). frames_analysis' C930e device_vs_host_ppm=+393 is wrong: OLS is biased by the start-up latency regime.
verdicts.numbers: pts_hz_from_gt_fit 30,001,037 / 299,998,822; envelope vs GT rate +28 / -4 ppm

verdicts.claim: Kiyo Pro: 0 frames, 21 MF errors
verdicts.reason: The session json records frames 0, errors 21, wall_s 0.009.
verdicts.numbers: 0 frames, 21 errors

result.corrected_statement: In this one 30 s run (1280x720@30 MJPEG, E assumed 2^-7 s), PTS-based timestamps for the C930e and C922 agree with the flash ground truth to 0.53-0.59 ms std after removing a per-source offset, using a GT built without any device timestamp and with an a-priori gamma of 2.2. A frame counter fitted to host arrival (seq_periodic_env) scores the same (0.53/0.58 ms). So does PTS at its nominal rate with only an offset (0.55/0.59 ms). Fitting PTS directly to the GT still leaves 0.49/0.59 ms, and the errors depend systematically on the brightness fraction. About 0.5 ms is therefore the method floor on real data: what can be asserted is that PTS error is ≤ ~0.5-0.6 ms and cannot be told apart from a perfectly periodic sensor. Host arrival and MF sample time are 4.7-5.1 ms std; that comparison is fair and robust. The 0.52 ms for uvc_pts_mapped_direct needs a hindsight whole-run fit. Causal or holdout mappings give 0.6-3.6 ms on the C930e, depending on how the 22.9 ms start-up latency regime is handled, and 0.59-1.1 ms on the C922. The cross-camera offset agreement is not evidence of sync accuracy: the quoted numbers are on a 0.02 ms grid, host arrival agrees equally, and the per-camera offset changes by 35 ms with ROI position. No ranking among the PTS variants and no multi-camera sync figure is supported.
harness_bugs: flash_analyze.py: the GT reference is the best-scoring source and gamma is tuned to minimise that source's own error, so the reference is scored on a GT tuned to itself (vs_GT std == its per_frame std). Use a fixed gamma and a reference independent of the judged sources.
flash_analyze.py: offset_ms (coarse correlation search on a 0.02 ms grid) sits next to vs_ground_truth.offset_ms. The claim quoted the coarse one as cross-camera agreement.

flash_analyze.py brightness model: step display, power-law tone curve and a fixed E give f-dependent errors up to about 1 ms (opposite sign for rising and falling edges). LCD response is not modelled, and the ~75 us synthetic floor does not transfer to real data.
flash_analyze.py: a GT offset is per-ROI, not per-camera (it varies by 35 ms across blocks). Cross-camera offset_diff compares ROIs at different sensor rows and screen positions.

flash_analyze.py load_display: presents without their own stats sample inherit the refresh offset from the previous stats sample (468 of 2160 have one), so glitches in between cannot be seen. Independent flip and composition on the rotated, non-primary monitor are not logged.

analyze_frames.py lower_envelope_fit: starts from OLS and fails on start-up latency regimes (C930e first-half fit is 1000 ppm off). uvc_pts_mapped_direct and the SCR-envelope variants are whole-run, non-causal fits.

analyze_frames.py: pts_freq_vs_host / device_vs_host_ppm use plain OLS against arrival, so the C930e +393 ppm is wrong (the GT gives +35 ppm). device_clock_hz is never read from the descriptors (nominal_assumed=true; the C922's 300 MHz is a guess).
analyze_frames.py periodic_fit: the periodogram locks onto 32.42 fps for C930e host_arrival and os_timestamp, so their residual_rms (5.1 ms) and drops_est (27-30) are artefacts.

Reproducibility: timing/build/*.exe were rebuilt at 14:38 and mf_uvc_timing.cpp / flash_timecode.cpp were modified 14:35-14:38, all after the 14:34 capture, so the binary that produced the data may not match the current source. analyze_frames.py was also edited during this check (only diagnostic fields added).

result.lens: Independent reproduction: re-ran the analysis on the original flash_run1_repositioned data, then ran the flash test fresh: 4 runs at exposure -7 (one of them C922-only and one C930e-only by accident), plus one each at -9 and -6. All runs used C922 + C930e at 1280x720@30 MJPEG, 30 s, timecode on monitor 0, and every capture ran under camlock. Snapshots taken first confirmed both cameras still see the portrait monitor 0.

verdicts.claim: The reported numbers reproduce from the existing flash_run1_repositioned data (flash_analyze.py and analyze_frames.py)
verdicts.reason: Re-running flash_analyze.py on the scratchpad flash1 data gives a flash_analysis.json identical to the committed one (358 of 358 numeric leaves). analyze_frames.py output differs only in device_clock fields, because the script has changed since: the C922 clock guess went from 1 GHz to 300 MHz and new fields were added. Per-source timing stats are identical. The synthetic selftest also reproduces exactly (66/66). Caveat: the claim mixes two kinds of number. Offsets are the coarse correlation-fit offset_ms (-52.08, -52.10, -61.06), not the vs_ground_truth medians (-51.84, -51.90, -60.01). The C922 0.45 ms is vs_GT, while its per-frame std is 0.52 ms.
verdicts.numbers: flash_analysis 0 diffs out of 358; frames_analysis 16 diffs, all in device_clock (nominal_hz, stc_minus_pts, ppm); selftest 0 out of 66

verdicts.claim: C930e uvc_pts_mapped_direct std 0.52 ms
verdicts.reason: The C930e PTS is a synthetic counter. It advances exactly 997222 ticks per frame (33.2407 ms at an assumed 30 MHz), but the real frame period measured from STC, SOF and host arrival is 33.275-33.280 ms in the fresh runs (33.228 ms in run1). So STC-PTS ramps from about 30 to 63 ms, and about once per 24 s the PTS jumps 2 periods with no gap in STC or host arrival. All 5 fresh C930e runs had one such step; run1 had none in its 30 s. A single whole-run lower-envelope line cannot follow it. Mapping PTS through the STC clock instead (uvc_pts_via_stc_line, a source I added) does better, at 0.37-4.3 ms.
verdicts.numbers: C930e mapped_direct vs-GT std: run1 0.52 ms; v1 10.28 ms (corr 0.789); v2a 4.83; v2(skip100) 5.24; exp-9 8.63; exp-6 8.54. PTS 2x step at frame index 721, 293, 730, 721 and 335.

verdicts.claim: C922 uvc_pts_mapped_direct std 0.45 ms (offset -52.10)
verdicts.reason: The std reproduces run to run, but it is not evidence that PTS carries timing information. A model with no metadata at all (seq_envelope: frame index fitted to the host-arrival lower envelope) and STC mapped directly give the same std in every run. In run1, seq_envelope also matches the C930e's 0.521 ms exactly. The C922 PTS has 125-137 us rms periodic jitter, yet both cameras land near 0.45-0.5 ms against ground truth. That points to the real-data method floor (LCD response, ROI, JPEG), about 6x the 75 us synthetic floor. The offset depends on the auto-ROI image row and is not stable across runs.

verdicts.claim: uvc_pts_via_scr_lsq_envelope std 0.48 ms (C930e, offset -21.0) and 0.50 ms (C922, offset -18.94)
verdicts.reason: C922 lands at 0.29-0.77 ms across runs. C930e is 1.0-4.3 ms in the fresh runs, except runs with very few qualifying frames (n=13 and n=25). The offsets move by several ms between runs. This source is also the ground-truth reference in most runs, and its gamma is tuned to minimise its own std, so its self-std is biased low.

verdicts.claim: host_arrival std 4.50/4.66 ms and MF os_timestamp 4.55/4.83 ms
verdicts.reason: The C922 values reproduce. On the C930e, the fresh runs are 2-2.5x worse because exposure-to-arrival latency follows the PTS sawtooth (about 33 ms peak to peak) when the device's sensor and output rates differ.

verdicts.claim: Cross-camera uvc_pts_mapped_direct offsets agree to 0.02 ms, so it is the best source for multi-camera sync
verdicts.reason: (a) The 0.02 ms comes from the coarse-fit grid (0.02 ms step). The JSON cross_camera field says +0.064 ms, and host_arrival agreed to +0.097 ms in the same run, so agreement does not single out PTS. (b) The fitted offset depends on which image row the ROI covers: 30.4-31.1 ms per frame height (rolling shutter), measured on both cameras with fixed ROIs. The two auto-ROIs sat at rows 0.93 (C930e) and 0.62 (C922), and at different screen columns, which matters because the portrait panel scans out across the image. Agreement in run1 is therefore unexplained, possibly coincidental. (c) Fresh runs do not reproduce it.
verdicts.numbers: C930e-C922 mapped_direct offset difference: run1 +0.064; v1 +7.40; v2 -4.18 (skip100 -1.40); exp-9 +3.84; exp-6 -14.72 ms. Row slope 30.4-31.1 ms per frame height on both cameras.

verdicts.claim: No dropped frames (891/893)
verdicts.reason: True for run1's delivered stream: seq is contiguous and there are no PTS gaps. In every fresh C930e run the PTS skips one period once per run, a sensor frame skipped or re-timed by the device. In v2a that coincided with an 80 ms host-arrival gap. Delivered-frame counts alone do not show this.
verdicts.numbers: C930e PTS steps: 0 in run1; 1 in each of v1, v2a, v2, exp-9, exp-6. Host gap at the step 32 ms (normal) or 80 ms (v2a) or 48 ms (exp-6).

verdicts.claim: Method floor on synthetic data about 75 us
verdicts.reason: The synthetic selftest reproduces exactly (74.8 us). But the simulation has no LCD response time, no rolling shutter and no exposure error. On real data, a pure frame-index model reaches the same about 0.45 ms as PTS, so the real floor is about 0.4-0.5 ms. The selftest also shows per-frame std under-reports noisy sources: 4.6 ms of injected noise is reported as 2.38 ms per-frame.
verdicts.numbers: Synthetic 74.8 us at sigma=0; injected 4600 us gives per-frame 2383 us and vs-GT 4460 us.

verdicts.claim: PTS marks exposure start (exposure test: does the offset shift by half the exposure change?)
verdicts.reason: C922 with the ROI held fixed (column 0.75, row 0.5): the exposure-start offset shifts by -1.13 to -1.34 times the exposure change, so PTS is locked near the end of exposure / readout, not the start. Raw auto-ROI flash_analyze output would wrongly suggest about 0.5x (mid-exposure), because the auto-ROI moved from row 0.43 to 0.72 between runs, a 31 ms per frame-height effect. Caveats: one run each at -9 and -6. The anchor is the arrival-envelope mapping; STC-PTS stays at 33.0 ms at every exposure. Assumed E is nominal 2^n. C930e: untestable, because at -9 its brightness did not change (median 98 vs 95.5), even though the control read back as manual -9.

verdicts.claim: Kiyo Pro: 0 frames, 21 MF errors at start in this tool
verdicts.reason: Not retested. The fresh runs left the Kiyo closed so as not to disturb other agents' tests; it cannot see the monitor anyway.

result.corrected_statement:
Rerunning the analysis on the original data gives exactly the same results. The fresh repeats do not support the conclusions.

C922 (6 runs, 3 exposures): the vs-ground-truth std is stable at 0.39-0.54 ms. Host arrival / MF os_timestamp are 3.9-5.3 ms. A metadata-free model gives the same 0.41-0.51 ms: host arrival's lower envelope fitted against frame index. So the 0.5 ms figure is the method floor on real data and shows that frames are periodic. It is not shown to be PTS accuracy. With the ROI held fixed, the C922 exposure-start offset is reproducible to sd 0.19 ms across 4 runs at E=7.81 ms. It shifts by about -1.1 to -1.3 times the exposure change (-50.97 / -58.83 / -67.64 ms at E = 1.95 / 7.81 / 15.63 ms). So the C922 PTS/arrival timing is locked near the end of exposure (readout), not the start; this rests on a single run each at -9 and -6.

C930e: its UVC PTS is a synthetic counter (fixed 997222 ticks per frame) that drifts about 0.1% against the real frame clock and jumps one extra period about every 24 s. Every fresh run (5/5) had a jump, which makes uvc_pts_mapped_direct 4.8-10.3 ms. Run1's 0.52 ms happened only because its 30 s held no jump. Mapping PTS through the STC clock reaches 0.4-1.8 ms, and 4.3 ms at E=15.6. C930e host arrival / os_timestamp are 8-12 ms in the fresh runs. The C930e did not visibly apply exposure -9.

The fitted offset depends on ROI row at 30.4-31.1 ms per frame height (rolling shutter), and the auto-ROI moves. Auto-ROI offsets are therefore not comparable across runs or cameras. The 'cross-camera offsets agree to 0.02 ms' claim does not hold: the file says 0.064 ms, host arrival agreed to 0.097 ms in the same run, and fresh runs give -14.7 to +7.4 ms. No uvc_pts_mapped_direct result supports multi-camera sync for the C930e. For the C922 it is equivalent to a frame-index model, and it needs a whole-run, non-causal fit.
harness_bugs: run_flash_test.ps1: the documented call is 'pwsh -File ... -Cams' with several cameras, but -File passes 'a','b' as ONE string. mf_uvc_timing then silently opens only the first camera (flash_verify_0_c922only). Workaround: flash_verify_tools/run_verify.ps1 builds the array inside PowerShell.

flash_analyze.py auto-ROI: the ROI picks a different image row each run (C922 0.43-0.72, C930e 0.93), and the fitted offset depends on row at about 31 ms per frame height (rolling shutter), and on column through display scan-out. Absolute offsets and the cross_camera block are not comparable across runs or cameras unless the ROI is fixed.

flash_analyze.py has no check that the flash was on screen. In flash_verify_2 the flash window was absent for the first ~3 s; those frames were silently included and corr dropped (C930e 0.66, C922 0.82).

flash_analyze.py ground-truth circularity: the reference is whichever source has the smallest self-std, with gamma tuned per source to minimise that same std. Per-frame std is biased low for noisy sources (selftest: 4.6 ms injected reported as 2.38 ms).
Synthetic selftest (75 us floor) lacks LCD response, rolling shutter and exposure mismatch. Real-data floor is about 0.4-0.5 ms (a frame-index model matches PTS).

analyze_frames.py uvc_pts_mapped_direct is one whole-run lower-envelope line (non-causal). It breaks on the C930e's synthetic PTS, which drifts 0.1% against the real frame clock and jumps 2 periods about every 24 s.

analyze_frames.py guesses the device clock (nominal_hz) instead of reading dwClockFrequency. The guess changed between script versions (C922 1 GHz to 300 MHz), so frames_analysis.json for the same data is not bit-reproducible.

mf_uvc_timing: exposure readback is not a check that the exposure was applied. C930e read back manual -9, but frame brightness did not change from -7. Gain is 'auto' in the request, yet reads back with the manual flag and a value that varies between runs (0, 4, 6, 9).

Claim reporting mixes the coarse-fit offset_ms (0.02 ms grid) with vs_ground_truth medians and std. The '0.02 ms cross-camera agreement' is a grid artifact; the file's own cross_camera value is 0.064 ms.
Transient 'no device matches' for the C922 at MF enumeration (flash_verify_2a), cause unknown, possibly concurrent agents. The device showed OK in Get-PnpDevice immediately after.

result.lens: Kiyo Pro failure in the MF timing tool, and side effects of the MetadataBufferSizeInKB0=5 registry change (plus Razer Synapse and LogiTune as factors)

verdicts.claim: Kiyo Pro: 0 frames, 21 MF errors at start in this tool (flash_run1_repositioned)
verdicts.reason: The count is real, but the framing is misleading. (1) The failure is not specific to this tool. In the same time windows every API fails on the Kiyo: my minimal MF SourceReader, OpenCV MSMF, OpenCV DSHOW, PyAV dshow, a raw DirectShow graph, KS IOCTL GETs, and plain USB GET_DESCRIPTOR. (2) '21 errors' is just the loop cap in mf_uvc_timing.cpp:271 (it breaks once errors exceed 20), not a measurement. (3) The tool prints the ReadSample HRESULT only to stderr, and capture.log and session.json never recorded it. The HRESULT is 0x8007001F (ERROR_GEN_FAILURE), returned about 9 ms into the first ReadSample. (4) Controls showed 'supported:false' because GetRange/Get failed (MF GetRange 0x80070490, Get 0x8007001F). The camera does have these controls: at 14:03 the same tool read them.
verdicts.numbers: Minimal MF probe at 15:05: 10 of 10 Kiyo attempts give activate 0x0, reader 0x0, SetCurrentMediaType 0x0, then ReadSample 0x8007001F x21 with 0 samples. Combos: MJPG 1280x720@30/60, 640x480@30, 640x360@30, 1920x1080@30/60; YUY2 640x480; NV12 640x480; H264 1280x720; MJPG 720p30 with no control queries. Same run: C922 82/82 samples, C930e 77/77.

verdicts.claim: (lens hypothesis) MetadataBufferSizeInKB0=5 breaks the Kiyo in Media Foundation
verdicts.reason: The Kiyo streamed through MF after the registry write (14:09:33), after re-arriving from a replug, with capture metadata attached to its samples. At 14:49:51 the mjpeg_msmf run (MF SourceReader) got 335 MJPG 1920x1080 frames from the Kiyo with read_error 0x0, and sample_attribute_dumps.json[1] shows MFSampleExtension_CaptureMetadata (MF_CAPTURE_METADATA_FRAME_RAWSTREAM) on its samples. SDL3's MF backend also got 151 valid MJPEG frames at 14:19 and gst mfvideosrc got 155 frames at 14:51. The failure is also not MF-specific: DirectShow, which never requests metadata, fails the same way, and so do non-streaming EP0 requests. A reg query shows the value only on the 6 intended keys (the 14:04 'noop' run left nothing on the NDI or Bluetooth keys).
verdicts.numbers: Kiyo in MF with metadata on: 335 frames at 14:49:51; SDL3/MF 151 frames at 14:19:22; gst mfvideosrc 155 frames at 14:51. Registry value present since 14:09:33.

verdicts.claim: (mechanism) Why the Kiyo fails: it stops answering control-endpoint (EP0) requests a few minutes after each (re)plug, and from then on every API fails
verdicts.reason: Tested directly, with MF, the Frame Server, usbvideo streaming and metadata all out of the path. (a) Asking the parent hub (IOCTL_USB_GET_DESCRIPTOR_FROM_NODE_CONNECTION) for the Kiyo's string descriptors 0 and iProduct fails with ERROR_GEN_FAILURE (31) in about 7 ms. The device descriptor, which the hub driver caches, still reads fine. C922 and C930e answer in under 0.1 ms. (b) KS IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY GET of CT exposure/focus and PU brightness/white balance on both the camera and capture interfaces fails with 31 in about 7 ms; on the C922 they succeed in 0.06-0.5 ms. History matches this: Kiyo strings were readable at 14:12:52 and 14:16:44 and failed at 14:34-14:36 (naming/descriptors.json, Errno 31). The pattern happened twice. Replug at 14:15:03, streaming OK until at least 14:19:29, failing by 14:31:12. Replug at 14:48:10, streaming OK at 14:49-14:51, failing by 15:03:56. A replug clears it for a few minutes; a vetoed pnputil restart did not. What triggers the wedge is NOT determined. Untested candidates: USB selective suspend or U1/U2 on the Genesys hub VID_05E3 PID_0625 that the SuperSpeed Kiyo sits behind; LogiTuneAgent, which holds a handle on the Kiyo (it vetoed the Kiyo's removal, event 225 at 14:11:20 and 14:33:09); some other agent's request; or Kiyo firmware. The event logs (System, Application, Kernel-PnP, USBXHCI) show nothing in either onset window. The FrameServer log has rolled over and no longer covers them.
verdicts.numbers: Kiyo string0/iProduct: win32 error 31, 7.06/7.01 ms. C922: 0.08/0.05 ms OK. C930e: 0.10/0.07 ms OK. KS CT/PU GET on Kiyo: 31, about 6.8-7.4 ms. Two onset windows: 14:19:29-14:31:12 and 14:51:18-15:03:56.

verdicts.claim: (lens task) Does the Kiyo stream MJPEG via OpenCV CAP_MSMF, CAP_DSHOW, PyAV dshow, or a minimal MF SourceReader, at 1280x720@30 and other modes, in its current state?
verdicts.reason: It does not stream through any of them right now; the failure is the same device state on every path. Exact results: minimal MF gives ReadSample 0x8007001F on all 10 combos. OpenCV 5.0 MSMF opens, but grab fails with -2147024865 (0x8007001F), 21 of 21 attempts. OpenCV DSHOW: isOpened false. PyAV dshow: 'Could not RenderStream to connect pins' at 1280x720@30 and 640x480@30. Raw DirectShow graph: bind 0x0, IAMCameraControl::Get 0x8007001F, SetFormat 0x0, RenderStream 0x80070057 for MJPG 720p30, MJPG 480p30 and YUY2 480p30. Controls run in the same hold: C922 streams in OpenCV MSMF (50 frames), OpenCV DSHOW (57), PyAV (62 packets) and the DShow graph (RenderStream 0x0, Run S_FALSE then running). The MF timing tool has no metadata-off switch, and none is possible from the app side: it only reads MFSampleExtension_CaptureMetadata after a sample arrives, and the failure happens at the first ReadSample. The --no-controls MF attempt fails identically.
verdicts.numbers: Kiyo: 0 frames on every backend and mode tried. C922 controls: MSMF 50, DSHOW 57, PyAV 62, DShow graph running.

verdicts.claim: C922/C930e behave differently with vs without metadata
verdicts.reason: No difference found in frame delivery at 1280x720@30. With metadata (MF, after the change), every sample carries CaptureMetadata: C922 82/82 and C930e 77/77 in my run, and 142/142 and 138/138 in meta_check1. Without metadata (MF at 14:03 before the change, and DShow/PyAV, which never request it) both stream normally. Host-arrival interval median is 32.0 ms in both conditions, p99 about 48 ms, with 0 errors. Controls read normally in both. These were short runs only (2-30 s), and I did not test a long soak or other modes.
verdicts.numbers: Before: C922 293 frames/10 s and C930e 290/10 s, 0 errors. After: C922 893/30 s and C930e 891/30 s (flash run), 0 errors. dt median 32.00-32.01 ms in both conditions.

verdicts.claim: Razer Synapse being closed, or LogiTune running, explains the Kiyo failure
verdicts.reason: Synapse: RazerAppEngine was killed at 14:11 and has not run since, yet the Kiyo streamed in MF and DShow at 14:16-14:19 and 14:49-14:51. So Synapse is not needed to stream, and closing it is not enough to cause the failure. LogiTuneAgent (pid 45784) was running in both the working and the failing windows, so as a standing condition it does not tell the two apart. The only effects I can show are the PnP vetoes (event 225), which leave devnodes in a pending-reboot state (MF_E_REBOOT_REQUIRED 0xC00D7167 at 14:10). Because it holds a handle on the Kiyo, it remains an untested candidate trigger for the EP0 wedge.
verdicts.numbers: Kiyo working with Synapse closed: PyAV 362 frames (14:17), SDL3/MF 151 (14:19), MF 335 (14:49), gst 155 (14:51).

verdicts.claim: (aside, timing claim) host_arrival std 4.50/4.66 ms reflects pipeline jitter
verdicts.reason: Outside this lens, but it showed up in the same frame logs: host-arrival intervals come in 16 ms steps (median 32.0 ms, p99 48 ms, so 32 or 48). Uniform 16 ms quantization alone gives a std of 16/sqrt(12) = 4.62 ms, which matches the reported 4.50/4.66 ms. That points to timer or delivery quantization, not jitter of the pipeline.

result.corrected_statement:
The Kiyo Pro got 0 frames in flash_run1_repositioned because of the device's state at that time. Neither the MF tool nor the MetadataBufferSizeInKB0 change is the cause. Twice today the Kiyo streamed for a few minutes after being replugged, then stopped answering control-endpoint (EP0) requests. Plugged in at 14:15:03, it streamed until at least 14:19:29 and was failing by 14:31:12. Plugged in again at 14:48:10, it streamed at 14:49-14:51 and was failing by 15:03:56.

In the failed state:
- Asking the hub for its USB string descriptors fails with ERROR_GEN_FAILURE (win32 error 31) in about 7 ms; C922 and C930e answer in under 0.1 ms.
- KS property GETs of the camera and image controls fail with 31.
- Every capture API fails: MF ReadSample returns 0x8007001F on all 10 subtype/mode combos (MJPG 720p30/60, 480p, 360p, 1080p30/60, YUY2, NV12, H264), OpenCV MSMF grab gets 0x8007001F, OpenCV DSHOW does not open, PyAV dshow gets 'Could not RenderStream', and a raw DirectShow graph gets RenderStream 0x80070057 with IAMCameraControl::Get 0x8007001F.

The Kiyo did stream in MF while the registry value was in effect: 335 MJPEG 1920x1080 frames at 14:49:51, with MFSampleExtension_CaptureMetadata on its samples. So the metadata setting does not break it. The C922 and C930e behave the same with metadata (100% of MF samples carry it) and without it (DShow, and the 14:03 baseline). Razer Synapse is not needed to stream: it has been closed since 14:11 and the Kiyo still streamed in both working windows. What triggers the EP0 wedge is unknown.

Proposed confirmation, which the user would run:
1. Replug only the Kiyo; change no registry.
2. Run `timing/build/usb_ep0_probe.exe` and `kiyo_ks_mf_probe.exe --ks-only` every 30 s for 20-30 min under camlock, with no other Kiyo traffic, to time when it fails.
3. Repeat with LogiTuneUpdaterService stopped and LogiTuneAgent exited.
4. Repeat with USB selective suspend disabled (elevated).
5. Only if the failure tracks the metadata setting in those soaks: run `timing/scripts/revert_uvc_metadata.ps1` elevated, replug, and repeat the soak.

The '21 errors' count is the tool's loop cap, not a measurement.
harness_bugs: timing/src/mf_uvc_timing.cpp:271 prints the ReadSample HRESULT only to stderr (first 3 errors) and stops after more than 20 errors. session.json and capture.log therefore record '21 errors' (a loop cap) and never the HRESULT, which is 0x8007001F.

timing/scripts/recover_restart_cameras.ps1:30 and recover_restart_cameras3.ps1:26 test need_restart with mask 0x01000000. That bit is DN_NT_DRIVER, which every devnode with a loaded driver has; DN_NEED_RESTART is DN_LIAR = 0x00000100 (SDK shared/cfg.h:185/225). So need_restart always reads True.

results/windows/Gerald/mjpeg_mf_blocked/devnode_status_1439.json reports DN_NEED_RESTART=true for devnode_status 0x0180600A, which does not have bit 0x100 set (same wrong mask; rust/tools/devnode_status.ps1 has since been fixed in its comment).
timing/flash_run1_repositioned/NOTES.txt says the Kiyo 'failed to stream in this run' without noting that every API was failing on the Kiyo during 14:31-14:44, so the result reads as tool-specific.

My own harness, fixed and rerun (run2 is the valid data): (a) the first ks_only_1.jsonl PU GETs failed with ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER (122) on all cameras because the output buffer was too small; the CT results from that run are valid. (b) The kiyo_lens_all.sh cv/av step failed because uv is not on PATH inside the bash that camlock spawns; it was rerun directly, giving cv_av.json. (c) OpenCV 5.0 MSMF rejects CAP_PROP_FOURCC passed as an open parameter ('can't set property 6') even on the C922, so open-params made every MSMF attempt fail; cv_msmf_v2.json opens first and sets properties after. (d) OpenCV MSMF returns False for the MJPG FOURCC set and delivers decoded BGR, so the OpenCV MSMF attempt is not a native-MJPEG test. (e) PyAV negotiated rawvideo for the C922 at 640x480 despite vcodec=mjpeg, and the libav log handler leaks a line from one attempt into the next.

Lock hygiene: on my first DirectShow attempt Git Bash rewrote `cmd /c` into `cmd C:/`, which started an interactive cmd that sat on camlock for about 10 minutes with no camera open, until I killed it. The rerun from PowerShell worked.
